- .claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py
  Line or code reference: 515-528 (main) and 322-332 (_terminal_age_hours)
  Problem: The `.claude/` copy runs `classify()` unconditionally on every `list_sessions` page, including intermediate paging runs whose results the pickup discards. Each intermediate run issues `gh api` reads for every session's PR/issue and calls `record_stalls()`, marking stalls as seen so the final run reports them `new: false` and skips their notifications. Additionally, `_terminal_age_hours` at line 326 does not cache failed `gh_api` reads, so a read failure for one session is repeated for every other session on the same PR or issue. Both defects are already fixed in the `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py` twin (intermediate-run short-circuit at lines 533-537; failed-read caching at lines 335-340) and wait for the `[claude-twin-sync]` copy. The `.claude/` copy is the one the pickup runs.
  Why it fails at runtime: With 10 pages of sessions, the pickup reads at most 9 intermediate pages' worth of PR/issue data twice (once here and once on the final run), and intermediate-page stalls are never notified because `record_stalls` marks them seen before the final run classifies them.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- .claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py (both copies)
  Line or code reference: 479-487
  Problem: The 10-page limit with no resume cursor across wakes can permanently starve sessions below that boundary. Each hourly wake starts `list_sessions` from the newest page (`mine: true`, no `after_id` on the first call), and `next_after_id` returns `None` once `pages >= max_pages` (line 482). If the first 10 pages contain only ineligible sessions (running, working, on a prompt, tied to open PRs, or not-ours titles), no archivable session is found, nothing is archived, and the eligible sessions on page 11 remain unreached. The next wake repeats the same 10 pages. Eligible sessions on page 11+ are never archived and their prompt stalls are never reported.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the first 10 pages hold ineligible sessions and no archivable session exists to drain the list, those deeper eligible sessions sit unreached indefinitely. The horizon check at line 485 further reduces the page count if any page spans sessions older than 14 days, making the window even narrower.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py
  Line or code reference: next_after_id (lines ~493-501) and the pickup's step 3a.2 paging loop
  Problem: The 10-page cap combined with the "newest-first, no persistent cursor across wakes" paging model can permanently starve older eligible sessions. Each hourly wake's initial `list_sessions` call (step 3a.1) starts with no `after_id`, so it always re-reads pages 1-10. When `pages >= max_pages` (10), `next_after_id` returns None, so the script exits without producing a cursor for the next wake. If the newest 1000 sessions contain any sessions that remain ineligible for archival — sessions bound to enabled Routines, sessions for open PRs, sessions for PRs merged less than `--grace-hours` ago, or sessions still classified as running/working — the script processes those same 1000 sessions on every wake and never advances to pages 11+ where older eligible sessions live. In a high-churn environment where new sessions enter the top of the list faster than ineligible ones become eligible, the eligible older sessions are never archived and prompt stalls there are never reported.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is the run-time behavior, not a static concern: the next wake re-runs the same first 10 pages and exits with zero archives. The 14-day horizon bound is the documented primary stop condition, but the 10-page cap preempts it whenever the system has more than 1000 sessions within the horizon. The plan's "backlog drains from the newest end" rationale assumes the newest 1000 eventually become eligible and the script can then advance, but that assumption breaks down when system churn keeps the newest window populated with fresh ineligible sessions.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
